study.title: Manipulation of and Sustained Effects on the Human Brain Induced by Different Modalities of Acupuncture: An fMRI Study
study.study_design: Within-subject crossover fMRI study with four sessions (MA, EA, TEAS, sensory control), randomized session order, combined block-designed and resting-state fMRI
study.population: Eighteen healthy, right-handed participants naïve to acupuncture (9 male, mean age-22 years, range-19 to 27)
study.inclusion_criteria: Healthy, right-handed participants naïve to acupuncture

extraction_notes.note: Table 5 (DMN) and Table 6 (SMN) for the sensory control condition in the DMN analysis states 'There was no statistically significant region in comparison of sensory control.' For SMN, the sensory control shows only decreased connectivity rows (premotor cortex and supplementary motor area). The exact rows for the sensory control SMN in Table 6 share coordinate values with EA and MA rows in the table – this appears to be a complex merged table layout in the PDF. The values extracted for sensory control SMN were read from the table structure with caution.

Table 6 as rendered in the PDF is a complex multi-column table. The 'sensory control' SMN decreased connectivity coordinate values appear to share rows with MA or EA values. Extracted values for sensory control SMN (premotor cortex R: 64 -6 34, t=-5.15, 20 voxels and supplementary motor area R: 4 8 62, t=-4.64, 18 voxels) were read from the table. There is a risk of mis-attribution given the table's OCR complexity.

Exact numeric values for deqi sensation subscales (soreness, numbness, fullness, heaviness, dull pain, mean deqi) by arm are shown in Figure 2A, 2B, and 2C but are not provided as numeric values in the text. Only relative comparisons and statistical significance are extractable.

The TEAS DMN decreased connectivity entry in Table 5 shows Cuneus L coordinate as '-4 -12 -104 4' which appears to represent x=-4, y=-12, z=-104 with 4 voxels. z=-104 is anatomically implausible for the cuneus. This may reflect an OCR error or misprint in the original table. Extracted as reported.

Exact numeric values for n_analyzed in each rest dataset per condition: sensory control n=16, MA n=15, EA n=15, TEAS n=14 (rest datasets); block-designed: sensory control n=15, MA n=14, EA n=15, TEAS n=15.
The study does not report any expectancy, credibility, or treatment guessing measures beyond noting that participants were naive to acupuncture.
No autonomic response data (heart rate, skin conductance) were collected or reported; the authors acknowledge this as a study limitation.

Figure S1 shows group maps for DMN and SMN before and after acupuncture stimulation; these are referenced as a DOC supplement and not available in the main PDF. Detailed individual ICA component statistics may be in the supplement.

The paper does not specify whether the 'TEAS' acupuncture modality was delivered by a HANS device at both ST-36 and the non-acupoint location simultaneously (as in EA) or only at ST-36. The description states 'The same locations were attached with electrode slices to the skin surface in the TEAS session,' implying both locations were stimulated.

Table 4 TEAS S1 vs BL shows the coordinate for 'middle temporal gyrus R' as '-52 -58 4'; the negative x-coordinate (-52) for a right hemisphere region is unusual. Extracted as reported from the table.

The paper states the block-designed run was '5.5 min' total and included two 1-min stimulation periods (S1, S2), a 1-min rest epoch between them, and a 1.5-min baseline. Total block time: 1.5 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4.5 min of accounted time; the remaining time may include transitions. This is noted for reproducibility.
PMID is not provided in the document. DOI is 10.1371/journal.pone.0066815.

The SC (sensory control) S2 table (Table 1) shows cerebellum R at coordinate '14 -74 -46' but the table cell may only show 'R 5.06 14 -74 -46 71'. Extracted as: x=14, y=-74, z=-46, t=5.06, voxels=71. Note that this entry has only one side listed (R) in the original table.
